title: Security and identity
task_statement: Choose the credential, the workspace scope, and the data controls for each caller. (Inference: task wording from repo lesson 7-2A, not from the exam guide)

components.name: API keys and workspace scope
components.first_principle: An API key is a bearer secret, so its scope and expiration limit the damage from a leak.

nodes.label: API key with scope and expiry

steps: Create the key in the Console and select its expiration.
Choose a service account key for shared or automated workloads.
Scope the key to one workspace when the workload needs only that workspace.
Store the key in a secrets manager, not in source code.
Send the key as a bearer token in the Authorization header.
Rotate the key before its expiration date.
Disable a suspected leaked key at once.
pros: A scoped key limits access to one workspace.
Expiration limits how long a leaked key works.
Identity-backed keys become invalid when their identity leaves the organization.
cons: A static key stays valid until it expires or is disabled.
The Console shows the full key once, so a lost key needs a new key.
Workspace keys are legacy keys and remain usable after their creator leaves.
use_when: A developer runs scripts with a personal key for their own work.
A shared service needs its own identity. Create a service account key.
do_not_use_when: A cloud workload has a platform identity. Use federation instead.
A team shares one key. The key acts as one person and breaks when that person leaves.

constraints.choice: Use a service account key for shared workloads.
constraints.combination: Rotate keys before their expiration dates.

constraints.choice: Scope keys to one workspace for each environment.
constraints.combination: Use separate workspaces for tenants that must not share usage.

constraints.choice: Choose a workspace region on Claude Platform on AWS when residency matters.
constraints.combination: Send inference_geo us for US inference on Claude 4.6 and later models.

constraints.choice: Review key status and expires_at with the Admin API.
constraints.combination: Use an Admin API key only for the admin endpoints.

native_services.text: Short-term bearer tokens have a 12-hour maximum and are the least preferred option.
SigV4 signed requests with IAM are the primary method, and API keys are also supported.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
native_services.text: Each request carries a Google OAuth 2.0 access token, and three IAM roles control access.
Foundry supports API keys and Microsoft Entra ID tokens, with Azure RBAC roles.

components.exam_tie: F4. Expect a leaked key or a shared key in a scenario. The credited answer uses a scoped, identity-backed key or federation. (Inference)
components.trap: A key in a prompt or a config file looks convenient, but the model reads the prompt and the file exposes the secret.
components.decision_rule: Use a scoped, time-limited, identity-backed key, and store it in a secrets manager.
components.exam_tip: A 401 authentication_error can mean a revoked, malformed, or expired key.

components.name: Workload identity federation
components.first_principle: A workload presents a signed token from its own identity provider and receives a short-lived Anthropic token in return.

nodes.label: Federation rule with scope and lifetime

steps: Register the identity provider as a federation issuer in the Console.
Create a federation rule with match conditions for the workload.
Set the authorization scope and the token lifetime in the rule.
The workload presents its signed JWT for a token exchange.
Anthropic checks the JWT signature and the rule match.
Anthropic returns a short-lived token bound to a service account.
The SDK refreshes the token before it expires.
pros: No static secret needs storage or rotation.
Tokens expire in minutes instead of never.
The SDK re-reads a rotated token file on each exchange.
cons: Federation is only as strong as the upstream identity provider.
Setup needs the admin, owner, or primary owner role.
Each environment usually needs its own issuer.
use_when: A CI job or Kubernetes workload already has a platform identity.
A production workload must avoid long-lived API keys.
do_not_use_when: A developer needs access for a local script. A personal key suits own development.
The identity provider publishes no key set. Anthropic cannot verify the JWT.

constraints.choice: The SDK starts a refresh 120 seconds before expiry.
constraints.combination: Expect one token exchange at each workload start. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set the scope in each rule to the least access the workload needs.
constraints.combination: The default scope is workspace developer, the same as a workspace API key.

constraints.choice: Register one issuer for each environment.
constraints.combination: Create a separate rule for each service account.

constraints.choice: Mint a fresh JWT for each exchange, because JWTs with a jti claim are single-use by default.
constraints.combination: Check the authentication history page when an exchange fails.

native_services.text: AWS STS outbound web identity federation is disabled by default and needs one enable command per account.
Bedrock uses IAM assumed roles, and AWS STS issues temporary credentials.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)
native_services.text: Google Cloud credentials for the caller identity authenticate requests.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
native_services.text: Each request carries a Google OAuth 2.0 access token with the cloud-platform scope.
Microsoft Entra ID tokens authenticate requests, and they typically expire after 1 hour.

components.exam_tie: F4. Expect a CI or Kubernetes scenario that asks for no static secret. The credited answer uses federation with a short-lived token. (Inference)
components.trap: A long-lived key in CI secrets looks simpler, but it is a static secret that stays valid until someone rotates or disables it.
components.decision_rule: Use federation when the workload has a trusted identity, and use a personal key only for development.
components.exam_tip: A jti_reused failure means the JWT was presented before, so mint a new JWT for the exchange.

components.name: Data retention and encryption
components.first_principle: A data control names who stores data, for how long, and which key protects it.

nodes.label: Stored data when a feature needs it

edges.label: no storage at rest under ZDR

steps: Check whether each feature is eligible for zero data retention.
Ask the account team to enable ZDR for the organization.
Expect 30-day retention for Covered Models, which sit outside ZDR.
Choose a customer-managed key in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault when the contract requires one.
CMEK enablement is permanent, so confirm the key plan first.
Keep activity logs for at least 30 days on a rolling basis.
pros: Under ZDR, Anthropic does not store prompts or responses at rest after the response returns.
A customer-managed key gives the customer control of the encryption key.
Platform logs record activity for investigations.
cons: The Console and some features sit outside ZDR.
A CMEK misconfiguration can cause permanent data loss.
CORS is not supported for ZDR organizations, so browser apps need a backend proxy.
use_when: Regulated data passes through the API and the contract forbids storage at rest.
A customer requires control of the encryption key.
do_not_use_when: Sensitive data flows through the Console playground. ZDR does not cover the Console.
The team has no key recovery plan for CMEK.

constraints.choice: Pick the inference geography and the workspace region that residency needs.
constraints.combination: US inference applies a 1.1 times pricing multiplier on Claude 4.6 and later models.

constraints.choice: Name one owner for each retention and key decision.
constraints.combination: Record the ZDR enablement date for audit. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep activity logs for at least 30 days.
constraints.combination: Turn on Data Access logs on Google Cloud, which are off by default.

constraints.choice: Use CMEK only where the contract requires it.

native_services.text: Data handling follows Amazon Bedrock data protection, and CloudWatch and CloudTrail log activity.
The retention policy matches the first-party API, and ZDR is available on request. A separate CMEK setup page covers this platform.

native_services.text: The retention policy matches the API, and ZDR is available on request. Data Access logs are off by default.

components.exam_tie: F4. Expect a regulated data scenario with a retention or key requirement. The credited answer names ZDR or CMEK and the account team step. (Inference)
components.trap: Platform logs look like a data control, but logs do not enable zero data retention.
components.decision_rule: Enable ZDR or CMEK only through the account team, after you confirm the eligible features.
components.exam_tip: CMEK enablement is permanent, so the answer confirms the key plan before the change.

flowchart TD
  A{Workload has a platform identity?} -->|Yes| B[Federation with short-lived token]
  A -->|No| C{Shared or automated use?}
  C -->|Yes| D[Service account key scoped to workspace]
  C -->|No| E[Personal key for own development]
  B --> F{Data must not be stored?}
  D --> F
  E --> F
  F -->|Yes| G[Request ZDR through account team]
  F -->|No| H[Set retention and key owner]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  I[Platform identity] --> W{Trusted issuer?}
  W -->|Yes| FD[Federation token]
  W -->|No| K[Scoped key]
  K --> X[Expiration and workspace]
  FD --> R[Short lifetime]
  R --> A[Audit log]
  X --> A
  Z[ZDR] --> D[Data controls]
